IMO, empty here is completely fine. As a user, I expect API to be intuitive. For example, `requestInvalidation(X) + requestInvalidation(Y)` is same as `requestInvalidation(X + Y)`. And in this sense `emptySet()` is zero element of this operation.

Also, it makes usage more clear, for example you don't need to handle the `requestInvalidation(someListOfFiles.filter { someCondition(it) })` separately.

I added a comment about behavior for empty `files` instead.
Thanks, I rewrote to the `Channel` (TIL, `ChannelIterator#hasNext` can be `suspend`) - looks simpler than flows.

I did not add unit performance test to verify what I did. Instead, I did checks on our performance tests - they found the degradation initially (when I merged partially enabled (by mistake) switcher to master) - CPP-52172. I hope the numbers below are conviencing enough for this review to be merged :)

These tests were checking (`*`) the time for "go to declaration" action - and they caught degradation by accident - they measured interval until "frontend daemon starts after navigation".

| | getScopes, Win | time.h, Win | getScopes, Linux | time.h, Linux |

| master, switcher off | 813 | 706 | 835 | 667 |

| branch, switcher on, no daemon fix | 877 | 918 | 789 | 781 |
| branch, switcher on, daemon fix | 816 | 684 | 755 | 641 |

Last line = current review state, line previous to it = current state without daemon fix: `contextsLoaded` no longer pushes back a pending daemon start.

unfortunately `cached == null` can mean that cached contexts existed, preferred context was inferred and cached, but later `cached` was gc-ed. So there is no guarantee that preferred context is not set in this case
posted a comment
also i'm not sure it's correct to just skip the file when `fresh == null` because of this.

apparently it's kinda expected that provider returns the actual value for the given file at all times. So if it returns "loading" then probably it is the current value and we should drop previous contexts

interface ContextResult  { // name TBD

let's maybe assert not-empty? I mean it might be non-obvious that emptyList is noop and not "invalidate everything"

Also, it makes usage more clear, for example you don't need to handle the `requestInvalidation(someListOfFiles.filter { someCondition(it) })` separately.

result might be stale by the time this runs. 

consider using `readAndBackgroundWriteAction`. it guarantees that the world hasn't changed after read-action finished

let's use LinkedHashSet here. It would save us from potential nasty ordering problems.
(a lot of places in platform already swiched to LHS, also kotlin's default is also LHS)

unfortunately `cached == null` can mean that cached contexts existed, preferred context was inferred and cached, but later `cached` was gc-ed. So there is no guarantee that preferred context is not set in this case
also i'm not sure it's correct to just skip the file when `fresh == null` because of this.

apparently it's kinda expected that provider returns the actual value for the given file at all times. So if it returns "loading" then probably it is the current value and we should drop previous contexts
